paint.explanation: {{title}}. Green cell: you play it and selected it. “−” sign: a hand from the {{t:range}} that's missing. “+” sign: selected, but the solver {{t:fold|folds}} it. Dot: a {{t:mixed-hand}} (the solver plays it only sometimes) or a disputed hand (the solver deviates from public charts on it), so it counts as correct either way. The score counts {{t:combo|combos}} ({{t:pair}} {{pairCombos}}, suited {{suitedCombos}}, offsuit {{offsuitCombos}}) only among hands in the {{t:range}} or selected.

range.wrongRare: The solver plays this only {{pct}} of the time, that is, almost never.
range.wrongVeryRare: The solver plays this with this hand less than {{pct}} of the time.
range.wrongNever: The solver never plays this with this hand.
range.mixedNote: This is a borderline hand: the solver mixes actions, so the app accepts as correct any answer played at least {{low}} of the time.
range.acceptableNote: An action played less than {{low}} but at least {{min}} of the time is acceptable: it's not a mistake, but the review will come back sooner.
range.freqRight: The solver plays this {{pct}} of the time, that is, {{often}}.
range.wrongOther: A weaker choice: {{status}}, but the solver usually plays it differently.
range.playMixed: You can play it or {{t:fold|fold}}, because {{status}}: the solver sometimes plays it and sometimes {{t:fold|folds}}.

status.in: in this situation this hand is within the {{t:range}}
status.out: in this situation this hand is outside the {{t:range}}
status.mixed: it's a hand on the edge of the {{t:range}}

often.overHalf: more often than every other time
often.underHalf: less often than every other time

reason.rfiUtg: There are still five players behind you, so someone more often has a better hand.
reason.rfiMid: The fewer players left behind you, the less often someone has a better hand and the more often you have {{t:position}} after the flop.
reason.rfiBtn: Only the blinds are left behind you, and after the flop you'll have {{t:position}}.
reason.rfiSb: You're now playing only against the {{t:big-blind}}, but after the flop you act first.
reason.nineEarly: At a 9-handed table there are more players behind you than at a 6-handed one, so someone more often has a better hand.
reason.nineLj: From the LJ you play as from {{t:utg|UTG}} at a 6-handed table, because the same number of players is left behind you.
reason.btnVsCo: Your opponent often {{t:call|calls}}, so you want a hand that plays well in a {{t:pot}} after a {{t:call}}.
reason.sbVsBtn: After a {{t:call}} from the {{t:small-blind}} you play {{t:out-of-position}}, and the {{t:big-blind}} behind you can still {{t:raise}}; a 3-bet gives you the {{t:initiative}} and a chance to win the {{t:pot}} right away.
reason.bbVsBtn: You add only a little to a big {{t:pot}}, so you defend wide.
reason.bbVsSb: After the flop you have {{t:position}}, so you realize more {{t:equity}}.
reason.pushSb: With a shorter stack you risk less relative to the blinds you win when your opponent {{t:fold|folds}}, and your opponent has to {{t:call}} wider.
reason.pushAnte: The ante makes the {{t:pot}} you win when your opponent {{t:fold|folds}} bigger, while the risk of the all-in stays the same.
reason.push3max: Each extra player behind you is another chance that someone wakes up with a strong hand, so everyone {{t:fold|folding}} happens less often.
reason.callBb: The caller wins only at showdown, and against a {{t:range}} that is already stronger than a random one; the player who {{t:shove|shoves}} also wins when the opponent {{t:fold|folds}}.
reason.call3max: The player behind you may have a strong hand and join in, and against two {{t:range|ranges}} your hand's {{t:equity}} drops quickly.
reason.call3maxTwo: Against two {{t:range|ranges}} your hand's {{t:equity}} drops quickly.
reason.pushSb3max: The Button has already {{t:fold|folded}}, so only the {{t:big-blind|big blind}} has to {{t:fold}}; from the Button, two players have to {{t:fold}}.
reason.pushSbDeep: With a deeper stack you risk more relative to the blinds you win when your opponent {{t:fold|folds}}, so you {{t:shove}} fewer hands than with a shorter stack.

hand.pair: You have a {{t:pair}}, a made hand before the flop: a hand without a {{t:pair}} needs help from the {{t:community-cards}} to beat it.
hand.high: Both cards are high: when you hit a {{t:pair}}, it is a high one, and your other card is a high {{t:kicker}} that usually beats weaker hands with the same card.
hand.suited: Your cards are suited: that is an extra way to win with a {{t:flush}}.
hand.connected_one: Your cards are close together: they can make a {{t:straight}} together in {{count}} way.
hand.connected_other: Your cards are close together: they can make a {{t:straight}} together in {{count}} ways.
hand.highAllIn: In an all-in there are no more {{t:bet|bets}} after the flop: if nobody has a {{t:pair}} or better, the higher card usually wins, and your higher card is {{rank}}.
hand.dominated: When you make a {{t:pair}} with your higher card ({{rank}}), an opponent with the same card and a better {{t:kicker}} usually beats you: this hand is dominated.
hand.overcards: Both cards are low: in {{pct}} of flops ({{often}}) at least one card higher than both of yours comes, and an opponent who pairs it has a higher {{t:pair}} than any pair from your cards.
hand.overcardsPair: Your {{t:pair}} is low: in {{pct}} of flops ({{often}}) at least one higher card comes, and an opponent who pairs it has a higher {{t:pair}}.

range.acceptableFreq: The solver plays this {{pct}} of the time, so it's not a mistake, but it more often chooses a different action. It's best to remember the more frequent one.

reason.kicker: The hand category is the same, so the first differing side card (kicker) in the best five decides.
reason.higherSameCategory: You both have {{hand}}, but one is higher.
reason.boardPlays: Both players' best five is on the {{t:board}}, so both are “{{t:playing-the-board}}” and it's a {{t:split-pot}}.
reason.identical: The best fives have the same ranks, so it's a {{t:split-pot}}.

outs.promptFlush: How many outs do you have to a {{t:flush}}?
outs.promptStraight: How many outs do you have to a {{t:straight}}?
outs.baseFlush: You have 4 cards of one suit. A suit has 13 cards, so 13 − 4 = 9 are left.
outs.baseOesd: You have 4 consecutive cards open on both ends. Each of the two missing ranks makes a {{t:straight}}, in 4 suits each: 8 cards.
outs.baseGutshot: You're missing one card in the middle of the {{t:straight}}. Only one rank completes it, in 4 suits: 4 cards.
outs.chanceFlop: {{base}} Chance on the turn: {{next}} ({{outs}} × 2 ≈ {{outs2}}). By the river, if you see both cards without paying more (e.g. after an all-in): {{river}} ({{outs}} × 4 ≈ {{outs4}}).

icm.table: {{players}} players, {{paid}} places paid ({{payouts}} of the {{t:prize-pool}}). Stacks: {{stacks}}.
icm.callPrompt: {{t:bubble|Bubble}}: {{table}} {{villain}} goes all-in; {{atRisk}} {{t:chips}} are at stake between you. Your hand has {{equity}} equity against their {{t:range}}. Ignore the blinds. What do you do?
icm.callRight: Yes. Your hand wins more often than the price on the {{t:bubble|bubble}} requires: you have {{equity}}, and under {{t:icm|ICM}} you need {{required}}.
icm.callWrong: No. Your hand wins too rarely even in a game for {{t:chips}}, and on the {{t:bubble|bubble}} the threshold is even higher: under {{t:icm|ICM}} you need {{required}}, and you have {{equity}}.
icm.callWrongChips: No. On the {{t:bubble|bubble}}, losing takes more of the {{t:prize-pool}} from you than winning adds, so you {{t:call}} only with a hand that wins clearly more often. Under {{t:icm|ICM}} you need {{required}}, and you have {{equity}}; in a game for {{t:chips}}, this {{t:call}} would be profitable.
icm.foldRight: Yes. Losing costs you more here than winning adds, and your hand wins too rarely: under {{t:icm|ICM}} you need {{required}}, and you only have {{equity}}.
icm.foldRightChips: Yes. Losing costs you more here than winning adds, and your hand wins too rarely: under {{t:icm|ICM}} you need {{required}}, and you only have {{equity}}. In a game for {{t:chips}}, this would be a {{t:call}}: that's exactly the {{t:risk-premium}}.
icm.foldWrong: Too tight. Even with the surcharge for risk on the {{t:bubble|bubble}}, your hand wins often enough: you have {{equity}}, and the threshold under {{t:icm|ICM}} is {{required}}.
icm.callExplanation: On the {{t:bubble|bubble}} you count in money, not in {{t:chips}}: losing takes {{loss}} of the {{t:prize-pool}} from you, while winning adds only {{gain}}. That's why you need about {{required}} equity, while in a game for {{t:chips}} {{requiredChips}} would be enough. The math: your equity in the {{t:prize-pool}} is {{now}} now, {{win}} after a win and {{lose}} after a loss; bubble factor = {{loss}} ÷ {{gain}} ≈ {{bf}}, threshold BF ÷ (BF + 1) ≈ {{required}}.
icm.equityPrompt: {{table}} What is your stack worth under {{t:icm|ICM}} (share of the {{t:prize-pool}})?
icm.equityRight: Yes. It's the sum over places: chance of the place × {{t:payout}} for the place.
icm.equityChips: No. That's your share of the {{t:chips}}. In a {{t:tournament}} with {{t:payout|payouts}}, {{t:chips}} don't convert to money one to one.
icm.equityFirstOnly: No. That's only the chance of 1st place × the {{t:payout}} for 1st place. Add the chances of the other paid places.
icm.equityExplanationMore: The chance of 1st place is your stack ÷ all {{t:chips}} ({{share}}); you calculate the next places the same way among the remaining players. In total {{icm}} of the {{t:prize-pool}}, more than your share of the {{t:chips}}.
icm.equityExplanationLess: The chance of 1st place is your stack ÷ all {{t:chips}} ({{share}}); you calculate the next places the same way among the remaining players. In total {{icm}} of the {{t:prize-pool}}, less than your share of the {{t:chips}}.

adjust.nit: You respect their {{t:raise|raises}} and 3-bets, {{t:fold}} hands from the bottom of your {{t:range}} more often, and steal their blinds more often.
adjust.regular: You play close to the baseline from modules 3–9 and deviate from it only when their stats show a clear mistake.
adjust.passive: More {{t:value-bet|value bets}}, including thinner ones, and fewer {{t:bluff|bluffs}}, especially on the river.
adjust.maniac: You don't {{t:bluff}} them, you {{t:call}} wider with hands that catch {{t:bluff|bluffs}}, and with a very strong hand you let them bet.
adjust.unknown: You play them like an unknown player, that is, by the baseline, and gather more hands.

potOdds.prompt: There's {{pot}} in the {{t:pot}}. Your opponent {{t:bet|bets}} {{bet}}. How much equity do you need to {{t:call}}?
potOdds.explanation: Your opponent {{t:bet|bets}} {{bet}} into a {{t:pot}} of {{pot}}. To {{t:call}}, you put in {{bet}}, and the whole {{t:pot}} after your {{t:call}} is {{total}}: you need {{required}} equity, that is, to win roughly once in {{needN}}. The math: {{bet}} ÷ {{total}} {{sign}} {{required}}.
potOdds.right: Yes: you divide what you put in by the whole {{t:pot}} after your {{t:call}}.
potOdds.mistakeNoCall: No. That's the {{t:bet}} divided by the {{t:pot}} after the {{t:bet}}. Add your own {{t:call}} to the denominator too.
potOdds.mistakeBetOverPot: No. That's the {{t:bet}} divided by the {{t:pot}} before the {{t:bet}}. Compare it with everything you can win.
potOdds.mistakeInverted: No. That's the {{t:pot}} before the {{t:bet}} divided by the {{t:pot}} after the {{t:bet}}, so the fraction is upside down. The top should be what you put in, and the bottom the whole {{t:pot}} after your {{t:call}}.

drawCall.promptFlop: Flop. There's {{pot}} in the {{t:pot}}, and your opponent {{t:bet|bets}} {{bet}}. You have {{draw}}. What do you do?
drawCall.promptTurn: Turn. There's {{pot}} in the {{t:pot}}, and your opponent {{t:bet|bets}} {{bet}}. You have {{draw}}. What do you do?
drawCall.whyFlop: What counts is the chance on one card, because you're only {{t:call|calling}} this {{t:bet}}: before the river you'll usually pay another price.
drawCall.whyTurn: What counts is the chance on one card: only one is left.
drawCall.situationFlop: You have {{draw}} on the flop, and your opponent {{t:bet|bets}} {{bet}} into a {{t:pot}} of {{pot}}.
drawCall.situationTurn: You have {{draw}} on the turn, and your opponent {{t:bet|bets}} {{bet}} into a {{t:pot}} of {{pot}}.
drawCall.decisionGood: You {{t:call}}, because your draw hits more often than the price requires.
drawCall.decisionNear: You {{t:fold}}, because your draw hits slightly less often than the price requires.
drawCall.decisionBad: You {{t:fold}}, because you'd be paying for a card that hits clearly less often than the price requires.
drawCall.priceFlop: The price: you need {{required}}, that is, to win roughly once in {{needN}}; the draw hits on the turn {{chance}} of the time ({{outs}} out of {{unseen}} unseen cards), that is, roughly once in {{hitN}}.
drawCall.priceTurn: The price: you need {{required}}, that is, to win roughly once in {{needN}}; the draw hits on the river {{chance}} of the time ({{outs}} out of {{unseen}} unseen cards), that is, roughly once in {{hitN}}.
drawCall.impliedFlop: It can pay off only thanks to implied odds, that is, when you win more after hitting, and provided the next price on the turn isn't too high either.
drawCall.impliedTurn: It can pay off only thanks to implied odds, that is, when you win more after hitting.
drawCall.callRight: Yes: the draw hits more often than the price requires, so a {{t:call}} makes money.
drawCall.callWrong: This {{t:call}} loses money: you pay {{bet}} for a card that hits less often than the price requires.
drawCall.foldRight: Yes: at this price the draw hits too rarely, so a {{t:fold}} saves {{bet}}.
drawCall.foldWrong: Too tight: the draw hits more often than the price requires, so a {{t:fold}} gives up a {{t:pot}} where a {{t:call}} makes money.

texture.scale: We count points: a {{t:straight}} possible in several ways (with at least two sets of two ranks) {{made}}, a {{t:straight}} possible in one way {{madeOne}}, only a {{t:straight-draw}} {{draw}}; a {{t:two-tone}} flop {{twoTone}}, {{t:monotone}} {{monotone}}. {{t:dry|Dry}} is 0–{{dryMax}}, medium {{medium}}, {{t:wet}} {{wet}} or more

height.high: a high flop's top card is an ace, king or queen
height.middle: a middle flop's top card is a jack or ten
height.low: a low flop's top card is a nine or lower

suits.rainbow: a {{t:rainbow}} flop has three cards in three different suits, so no one has a {{t:flush-draw}} yet
suits.twoTone: a {{t:two-tone}} flop has two cards of one suit, so a player's two cards of that suit make a {{t:flush-draw}}
suits.monotone: a {{t:monotone}} flop has all three cards of one suit, so a {{t:flush}} is already possible

ranks.paired: a {{t:paired}} flop has two or three cards of the same rank; a {{t:straight}} using a player's two cards is then impossible, though a {{t:straight-draw}} is sometimes possible
ranks.connected: a {{t:connected}} flop has three different ranks within five consecutive ones, so a {{t:straight}} is already possible (the ace also counts as one)
ranks.semiConnected: a {{t:semi-connected}} flop has two ranks within five consecutive ones, but not three: there's no {{t:straight}} yet, but a {{t:straight-draw}} (open-ended or gutshot) is already possible
ranks.disconnected: a {{t:disconnected}} flop has ranks so far apart that no two fit within five consecutive ones, so no one has even a {{t:straight-draw}}

wetness.wet: a {{t:wet}} flop gives many {{t:draw|draws}} or made {{t:straight|straights}}. {{scale}}
